title: Tiered autoscaling and regional fallback policy for reranker stability
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The reranker endpoint shows large tail latency and occasional region-level outages under bursty query patterns. Customers report slow search experiences and elevated error rates when a single region loses capacity. We need a resilient multi-dimensional approach that preserves relevance quality where possible while guaranteeing availability and bounded latency.

Goals: 1) Reduce p99 tail latency by 20-40% under production-like burst traffic. 2) Eliminate region blackout customer-visible errors by providing graceful fallbacks. 3) Keep average cost increase under 10% through tiered fallbacks and smarter autoscaling. 4) Provide clear observability and traces for any fallback decisions.

Design summary: 1) Tiered fallback engine: implement policy-driven fallbacks that degrade from full-rank GPU-serving reranker -> quantized CPU/GPU light reranker (smaller model) -> embedding-similarity rerank (ANN + cheap model) -> lexical heuristics. Policies are per-customer and per-route and can be time-bound. 2) Horizontal autoscaler enhancements: introduce predictive scale-up using EWMA of incoming concurrency and KV cache hit-rate, plus slow-start scaling to prevent oscillation. Add per-tenant concurrency ceilings to avoid noisy-neighbor storms. 3) Region-aware routing: preferred-region affinity by default; on region capacity pressure or degraded health decisions, automatically route to warm standby regions where latency delta < configured threshold. 4) Adaptive timeout & hedging: soft timeout for primary request with hedged fallback probe (sent at T_soft = 60% of SLO) to reduce tail latency. 5) Circuit breaker states: CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN per model variant + per-region, with exponential backoff and forced cooldown. 6) Quality-aware promotion: fallback quality is assessed via continuous evals on a small golden set; only allow promotion for a customer if quality drop is within configured tolerance.

Trade-offs and constraints: - Increased system complexity and more components to observe and maintain. - Fallbacks may produce lower relevance; mitigated by per-customer tolerances and tagging outputs. - Predictive scaling requires a short warm-up window for GPU-backed pools; fallback to light-reranker reduces user-visible impact while scale completes. - Cost: keeping warm standby regions adds cost; we will quantify in rollout.

Instrumentation and metrics: - New metrics: rerank.fallback.count (labels: reason, customer, region), rerank.p95/p99.latency (per-region, per-model), rerank.quality.delta (A/B golden set), rerank.circuit_breaker.state (per-region,variant). - Dashboards: rerank-stability overview (link below). - Alerts: >0.5% fallback rate for top 10 customers OR p99 > 350ms for 10m.

Artifacts and references: - Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/987654321/Tiered+Autoscale+and+Fallbacks+for+Reranker - Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerank-stability - Prototype PR (light-reranker + policy engine): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/387 - Canary run results (internal): https://internal.redwood.ai/experiments/rerank/2026-03-04-canary
acceptance_criteria: p99 reranker latency reduced by >=30% under synthetic production burst (replicates 10k QPS across 3 regions)
During simulated single-region outage, overall request success rate >= 99% and no customer-facing 5xx spikes
Fallbacks are auditable: every fallback decision emits trace/span with reason and quality tag
Per-customer fallback configuration is supported in console and respects quality tolerances
Canary run completed and rolled to 10% traffic with no regression in customer golden-set relevance beyond threshold
metrics: fallback_rate_sla: <1% for top-tier customers under normal load
acceptable_quality_drop: <=4% MRR (mean reciprocal rank) on golden set during fallback

comments: 2026-02-21 - Initial scoping with PM and SRE. Decided to prioritize tiered fallbacks over immediate global scale-up to limit cost. Action: Maya to draft design doc.
2026-02-28 - Prototype embedding-similarity fallback showed median latency 20ms but quality drop around 6% on one benchmark. Need golden-set-driven per-customer thresholds. (See PR #387)
2026-03-04 - Canary started: 2 non-critical customers at 5% traffic. Observed 12% fallback rate for one noisy tenant; added per-tenant concurrency cap in autoscaler (Arjun).
2026-03-09 - SRE review: suggested adding half-open probe delay and stronger circuit-breaker cooldown for region failover. Implemented in autoscaler branch.
2026-03-11 - UX/PM feedback: require console toggle to opt-out of automated fallback promotion. Added config flag and will include in release notes.
2026-03-12 - PR 412 opened for region-aware routing glue and hedging; requesting reviews from @sylvia and @tom. Running extended load test tonight.
